say.en: Two sales executives have the same salary. One meets every target and helps new staff; the other does the minimum. A fair firm must notice the difference, and pay for it. In this lesson: Explain the meaning and purposes of performance appraisal.
Describe traditional and modern methods of appraisal.
Distinguish time rate and piece rate, and wages and fringe benefits.

body.en: *Performance appraisal* is the systematic evaluation of an employee's performance and potential against set standards. It is used for promotion, transfer, pay increases, training needs and feedback. Traditional methods include ranking (arranging employees from best to worst), paired comparison, grading against defined categories, rating scales, checklists and critical incidents. Modern methods include management by objectives (MBO), in which manager and employee agree on goals and later review results; 360-degree appraisal, which collects feedback from superiors, peers, subordinates and customers; and behaviourally anchored rating scales.

points.en: Traditional: ranking, paired comparison, grading, rating scales, checklists, critical incidents
*Appraisal* should be objective, regular and discussed

body.en: *Compensation* is everything an employee receives for work: basic pay, allowances, incentives and fringe benefits. Under a time-rate system pay depends on time worked; it is simple and secure, suits work where quality matters, but gives no reward for extra output. Under a piece-rate system pay depends on output; it rewards efficiency but may hurt quality. A differential piece rate pays a higher rate to workers who reach a standard. Incentives may be financial (bonus, commission, profit sharing) or non-financial (recognition, job security). Fringe benefits include provident fund, medical care, housing and leave.

points.en: Differential piece rate rewards reaching the standard
Fringe benefits: PF, medical, housing, leave

problem.en: A worker can earn ₹600 a day on time rate, or ₹15 a unit on piece rate. With a differential scheme the rate rises by 40% for all units if output reaches 40 a day. Compare earnings at 38 and 42 units.

steps.en: At 38 units: piece wage = 38 × 15 = ₹570, below the time wage of ₹600.
At 42 units with the differential: rate = 15 × 1.4 = ₹21; wage = 42 × 21 = ₹882.
Ordinary piece rate at 42 units would give 42 × 15 = ₹630.
The differential gives a strong reason to reach the standard of 40.

answer.en: ₹570 at 38 units; ₹882 at 42 units under the differential rate (₹630 without it).

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. A worker can earn ₹600 a day on time rate, or ₹15 a unit on piece rate. With a differential scheme the rate rises by 40% for all units if output reaches 40 a day. Compare earnings at 38 and 42 units.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. A worker can earn 600 rupees a day on time rate, or 15 rupees a unit on piece rate. With a differential scheme the rate rises by 40 percent for all units if output reaches 40 a day. Compare earnings at 38 and 42 units.
At 38 units: piece wage equals 38 times 15 equals 570, rupees below the time wage of 600 rupees.
At 42 units with the differential: rate equals 15 times 1.4 equals 21 rupees; wage equals 42 times 21 equals 882 rupees.
Ordinary piece rate at 42 units would give 42 times 15 equals 630 rupees.
The differential gives a strong reason to reach the standard of 40.
So the answer is 570 rupees at 38 units; 882 rupees at 42 units under the differential rate 630 rupees without it.
